The effectiveness of trastuzumab deruxtecan outside clinical trials remains incompletely characterized for HER2-low metastatic breast cancer. We evaluated treatment patterns, clinical outcomes, and safety in a multi-institutional real-world cohort

We retrospectively identified consecutive adults with HER2-low metastatic breast cancer who initiated trastuzumab deruxtecan between 2021 and 2025 across six oncology centers. Demographic, clinicopathologic, treatment, and outcome data were abstracted from electronic records using a common data model. The primary endpoint was real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS); secondary endpoints included objective response rate (ORR), overall survival (OS), treatment duration, and grade 3 or higher adverse events. Time-to-event outcomes were estimated using Kaplan–Meier methods

The analysis included 286 patients with a median age of 61 years; 98% were female and the median number of prior systemic treatment lines was two. After a median follow-up of 18.4 months, ORR was 47.2%, median rwPFS was 8.7 months, and median OS was 21.3 months. Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 24.1% of patients. Interstitial lung disease was documented in 7.0%. In exploratory subgroup analysis, patients with IHC 2+/ISH-negative disease had a median rwPFS of 10.2 months

In routine practice, trastuzumab deruxtecan demonstrated clinically meaningful activity in HER2-low metastatic breast cancer, with outcomes generally consistent with its established treatment role. Toxicity remained manageable, although monitoring for interstitial lung disease is warranted. These findings support continued real-world evaluation in broader and underrepresented patient populations. Research Sponsor: None.

Patients hospitalized with breast cancer frequently have complex medical comorbidities, but the clinical impact of concurrent heart failure is not well defined. We examined inpatient outcomes and resource utilization associated with this complication

We analyzed the National Inpatient Sample for 2017–2022. Adult hospitalizations with a diagnosis of breast cancer were identified using ICD-10-CM codes and stratified by the presence or absence of heart failure. Weighted national estimates were generated. Multivariable logistic and linear regression models adjusted for age, sex, race, payer, hospital characteristics, metastatic disease, and comorbidity burden

Among an estimated 184,230 hospitalizations for breast cancer, 16,844 included heart failure. Patients with the complication had a median age of 69 years, and 97.8% were female. Mean length of stay was 6.1 versus 4.0 days, and mean hospital charges were $78,210 versus $55,240. After adjustment, heart failure was associated with higher odds of cardiogenic shock (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 12.8), acute respiratory failure (aOR 3.1), and in-hospital mortality (aOR 2.4)

Concurrent heart failure identifies a clinically vulnerable subgroup of hospitalized patients with breast cancer and is associated with greater morbidity, mortality, and resource use. Early recognition and coordinated oncologic and medical management may improve inpatient care. Research Sponsor: None.

Acquired resistance to sacituzumab govitecan in metastatic breast cancer may involve dynamic changes in therapeutic targets and associated signaling pathways. We evaluated longitudinal changes in TROP2 using paired tumor samples collected before treatment and at disease progression

Institutional databases were queried to identify patients with metastatic breast cancer who received sacituzumab govitecan and had paired pretreatment and post-progression biopsies. Samples were assessed by quantitative immunofluorescence and targeted proteomics. Marker abundance was compared within patients, and associations with clinical outcomes were explored using nonparametric tests

Paired samples from 32 patients passed quality control. Median progression-free survival on therapy was 5.8 months. Baseline TROP2 expression was 2,140 normalized units, with a median on-treatment change of −24%. Substantial loss of TROP2 was observed in 12 patients, whereas the remaining samples showed stable or increased expression. Top1 changed by −18% across paired samples (p=0.08). The aggregate pattern was consistent with heterogeneous target modulation rather than uniform antigen loss

Longitudinal changes in TROP2 after sacituzumab govitecan were heterogeneous in metastatic breast cancer. Resistance was not explained by a single uniform biomarker shift, supporting multi-analyte assessment of paired samples and further mechanistic study. Research Sponsor: Translational Oncology Fund.
